body.statement: For every period-specific row \(e\), every candidate nuisance \(\widetilde\eta=(\widetilde p,\widetilde m)\) with retained propensities clipped below by \(\varepsilon/2\), and the signal in Definition \(\ref{def:orthogonal-complete-normal-signal}\), the conditional drift is exactly a sum of propensity--regression products. Consequently its Gateaux derivative with respect to either nuisance at the truth is zero. Under the observable period-specific equalities, \(g_e(X)=0\) and \(S_e(O;\eta)=Z^{\mathrm{per}}_{e,P}(O)\) almost surely. Moreover, \[\|E_P[S^{\mathrm{per}}(O;\widetilde\eta)\mid X]-g(X)\|_{P_X,2}\le C_\varepsilon\|\widetilde p-p\|_{P_X,4}\|\widetilde m-m\|_{P_X,4}.\]
body.justification: The complete-normal correction must remain orthogonal after regression centering is estimated.
body.gap: A raw plug-in residual contrast has first-order regression-centering drift; adding the estimated restriction level cancels it algebraically.
body.consumer: The finite-support canonical estimator and its complete-normal moment-rate proposition use this product-bias identity.
